tweaks.err.service_start_type: Could not change the startup type of service {name}
tweaks.block.no_adapter: No network adapter with an IP address was found.
tweaks.block.sysmain_hdd: The system disk is an HDD: SysMain noticeably speeds up app launches on it, so it is better not to disable it.
tweaks.block.sysmain_unknown: Could not confirm that the system disk is an SSD, so disabling is unavailable.
tweaks.detail.hvci_never_on: Memory integrity has never been enabled on this PC, so the switch is already on.
tweaks.block.hvci_policy: Memory integrity is set by Group Policy and cannot be changed from here.
tweaks.game_dvr.title: Xbox Game DVR / background recording
tweaks.game_dvr.desc: Turns off background gameplay recording via Xbox Game Bar — it can use CPU and disk resources while you play.
tweaks.game_bar_off.title: Disable Game Bar and its overlay
tweaks.game_bar_off.desc: Game Bar will no longer open with the Xbox button on a gamepad or show its startup tip, and game recording and broadcasting are disabled by policy. Pressing Win+G manually may still open an empty panel.
tweaks.game_mode.desc: Built-in Windows mode that gives the game priority over background processes and updates while it runs.
tweaks.fullscreen_opt_off.title: Fullscreen optimizations (global)
tweaks.fullscreen_opt_off.desc: Turns off Windows' fullscreen handling for all games at once — in some games this gives a more stable frame rate in true fullscreen mode.
tweaks.fullscreen_opt_off.risk: Alt+Tab may become slower in some games.
tweaks.gpu_scheduling.title: Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling
tweaks.gpu_scheduling.desc: Hands frame queue management to the graphics card instead of the CPU. Improves performance on some systems, may cause instability on others — depends on the graphics driver.
tweaks.game_scheduler_priority.title: Game priority in the task scheduler
tweaks.game_scheduler_priority.desc: Raises CPU and GPU queue priority for games in the Windows multimedia scheduler profile (SystemProfile\Tasks\Games: GPU Priority, Priority, Scheduling Category).
tweaks.system_responsiveness.title: SystemResponsiveness for multimedia
tweaks.system_responsiveness.desc: Reduces the share of CPU that Windows reserves for background services in favor of multimedia and game threads (SystemResponsiveness = 10).
tweaks.network_throttling_off.title: Disable network throttling for multimedia
tweaks.network_throttling_off.desc: While music or video is playing, Windows artificially limits network packet processing. NetworkThrottlingIndex = ffffffff removes this limit.
tweaks.network_throttling_off.risk: On weak PCs, audio may occasionally stutter during large downloads.
tweaks.foreground_priority.title: Active window priority
tweaks.foreground_priority.desc: Win32PrioritySeparation = 0x26: the program you are working with right now (the game) gets longer and more frequent CPU time slices than background ones.
tweaks.foreground_priority.risk: Background tasks (archiving, rendering, downloads) will run a bit slower while you play.
tweaks.power_throttling_off.title: Disable Power Throttling for background apps
tweaks.power_throttling_off.desc: Windows slows down "unimportant" background apps to save power. Disabling removes this slowdown for all apps — useful if streaming, recording or voice chat run in the background while you play.
tweaks.power_throttling_off.risk: On a laptop running on battery, the charge will last less and the case may get warmer.
tweaks.mpo_off.title: Disable MPO (Multiplane Overlay)
tweaks.mpo_off.desc: Helps if you see flickering, black flashes or short freezes in games and the browser — especially with several monitors at different refresh rates. If you have no such problems, it won't help. May have no effect on the latest Windows 11 builds.
tweaks.mpo_off.risk: GPU load may increase slightly in windowed mode and video.
tweaks.hvci_off.title: Disable Core Isolation (Memory Integrity, VBS/HVCI)
tweaks.hvci_off.desc: Memory integrity checks drivers using virtualization. Turning it off may give a few percent more FPS but lowers Windows protection.
tweaks.hvci_off.risk:
• Malicious or vulnerable drivers will be able to get into the system kernel — this is exactly the attack this feature protects against.
• Some anti-cheats and games check system protection and may refuse to start or ask you to turn it back on.
• The FPS gain is small (a few percent) and not on every PC.
• The change takes effect only after a restart.
tweaks.nagle_off.title: Disable Nagle's algorithm
tweaks.nagle_off.desc: Windows bundles small network packets together and waits a little with acknowledgements. TcpAckFrequency = 1 and TCPNoDelay = 1 on active adapters remove this wait — may lower latency in older online games that use TCP. Most modern games use UDP, so this won't help them.
tweaks.nagle_off.risk: Slightly more small packets on the network; on slow or mobile internet, downloads may get slower. A new adapter (another Wi-Fi) won't be affected — you'll need to enable the tweak again.
tweaks.delivery_optimization_p2p_off.tit: Disable P2P sharing of Windows updates
tweaks.delivery_optimization_p2p_off.des: Delivery Optimization shares already downloaded updates with other computers and pulls them from other PCs, using your bandwidth. After disabling, updates come only from Microsoft servers — updates themselves work as before.
tweaks.mouse_accel.title: Mouse acceleration (Enhance pointer precision)
tweaks.mouse_accel.desc: Removes cursor acceleration so mouse movement is equally predictable at any speed — important for aiming accuracy in games.
tweaks.keyboard_repeat.title: Minimal delay and maximum key repeat rate
tweaks.keyboard_repeat.desc: A held key starts repeating almost immediately and at the highest rate (KeyboardDelay = 0, KeyboardSpeed = 31). Takes effect immediately.
tweaks.sticky_keys.title: Sticky, Filter and Toggle Keys shortcuts
tweaks.sticky_keys.desc: Prevents accessibility windows (Sticky/Filter/Toggle Keys) from popping up when you press Shift repeatedly, hold keys or press Num Lock during a game.
tweaks.transparency.title: Interface transparency
tweaks.transparency.desc: Turns off the transparency effect for windows, the Start menu and the taskbar.
tweaks.window_menu_anim.title: Window and menu animations
tweaks.window_menu_anim.desc: Turns off minimize/maximize window animations and menu appearance animations.
tweaks.shadows_taskbar_anim.title: Shadows, smoothing and taskbar animation
tweaks.shadows_taskbar_anim.desc: Turns off the shadow under icon labels, translucent selection in lists and taskbar button animations.
tweaks.menu_show_delay.title: Menu show delay
tweaks.menu_show_delay.desc: Removes the pause before submenus open (MenuShowDelay = 0).
tweaks.visual_fx_performance.title: Visual effects: "best performance"
tweaks.visual_fx_performance.desc: Switches the overall Windows visual effects preset to "Adjust for best performance" in the system performance options.
tweaks.tips_ads.title: Tips and ads in Start and on the lock screen
tweaks.tips_ads.desc: Removes ad tiles, tips and app suggestions in the Start menu and on the lock screen.
tweaks.advertising_id.title: Advertising ID
tweaks.advertising_id.desc: Prevents apps from using the advertising ID for personalized ads.
tweaks.bing_search.title: Bing search in the Start menu
tweaks.bing_search.desc: Turns off Bing web results when searching from the Start menu.
tweaks.background_apps.title: Background apps
tweaks.background_apps.desc: Prevents Microsoft Store apps from running in the background. May affect notifications of some apps (mail, messengers).
tweaks.telemetry.title: Windows telemetry
tweaks.telemetry.desc: Reduces the amount of diagnostic data Windows sends to Microsoft to the minimum level. On Windows Home/Pro it may not turn data collection off completely.
tweaks.hibernation_off.title: Disable hibernation
tweaks.hibernation_off.desc: powercfg -h off: deletes the hiberfil.sys file on drive C: (usually several gigabytes). Sleep works as before; only "Hibernate" and "Fast startup" disappear (the PC starts from scratch after shutdown — which is even more reliable).
tweaks.search_indexing_off.title: Disable search indexing
tweaks.search_indexing_off.desc: Stops the Windows Search service, which constantly scans files for fast search. Less background disk and CPU activity.
tweaks.search_indexing_off.risk: Search in the Start menu and File Explorer will become noticeably slower, and search in Outlook mail may not work.
tweaks.sysmain_off.title: Disable SysMain (SSD only)
tweaks.sysmain_off.desc: SysMain (formerly Superfetch) preloads frequently used apps into memory. On an SSD this barely speeds up launches but causes background disk access. Available only if the system disk is an SSD.
tweaks.sysmain_off.risk: Apps you haven't used for a long time may take a bit longer to open the first time.
tweaks.edge_startup_boost_off.title: Disable Startup Boost in Edge
tweaks.edge_startup_boost_off.desc: Edge will no longer start hidden in the background together with Windows. It is set by policy, so Edge will show "Your browser is managed by your organization" — this is normal.
tweaks.widgets_copilot_off.title: Disable widgets and Copilot on the taskbar
tweaks.widgets_copilot_off.desc: Removes the widgets panel (news, weather) and the Copilot button from the taskbar — they keep their own web content processes running in the background.
tweaks.show_hidden_ext.title: File extensions and hidden files
tweaks.show_hidden_ext.desc: Shows file extensions and hidden files and folders in File Explorer.
tweaks.no_auto_suggested_apps.title: Automatic installation of suggested apps
tweaks.no_auto_suggested_apps.desc: Prevents Windows from installing apps it "recommends" on its own.
tweaks.link.notifications.title: Notifications while gaming and in fullscreen
tweaks.link.notifications.desc: Windows 11 stores "Do not disturb" rules in a binary format that cannot be reliably changed from the registry, so there is no switch here. Open "Notifications" → "Turn on do not disturb automatically" and keep "When playing a game" and "When using an app in full-screen mode" enabled.
tweaks.game_mode.title: Windows Game Mode
proc.anticheat_warning: This is an anti-cheat. Don't close it before or during a game — otherwise the game won't start or you'll be kicked from the match.
proc.memory_compression.desc: Windows compressed memory: the system "packs" data here that doesn't fit into RAM.
proc.memory_compression.tip: If it's large (over 1 GB), you're short on RAM: close the browser or turn on Game Mode.
proc.system.desc: Windows kernel: drivers and device handling.
proc.system.tip: High load usually means a faulty driver — update your graphics card and chipset drivers.
proc.registry.desc: The Windows registry in memory — the settings database of the system and apps.
proc.registry.tip: Nothing to do, this is a normal process.
proc.svchost.desc: A container for Windows services (updates, network, sound, etc.). There are always many of these processes.
proc.svchost.tip: Don't close it. If one of them loads the CPU for a long time, it's often Windows Update — just wait.
proc.dwm.desc: Window manager: draws everything you see on the screen, including animations and transparency.
proc.dwm.tip: Don't close it — the picture will disappear. The load grows with the number of monitors and refresh rate.
proc.explorer.desc: Windows Explorer: taskbar, Start menu, desktop and folder windows.
proc.explorer.tip: If the taskbar is frozen, it can be restarted, but not simply closed.
proc.csrss.desc: A critical Windows service that manages console windows and shutdown.
proc.csrss.tip: Closing it will instantly cause a "blue screen".
proc.lsass.tip: Closing it will restart the computer.
proc.services.desc: Starts and stops all Windows services.
proc.services.tip: Don't touch it — the system won't work without it.
proc.wininit.desc: Starts the core Windows processes during system startup.
proc.wininit.tip: Don't touch it — closing it will crash the system.
proc.winlogon.tip: Don't touch it — it's part of the Windows sign-in.
proc.smss.desc: Session manager — one of the first to start when Windows boots.
proc.smss.tip: A normal system process, nothing to do.
proc.msmpeng.desc: Windows Defender antivirus: scans files as they are opened and downloaded.
proc.msmpeng.tip: If games stutter, add your games folder to Defender exclusions, but don't turn protection off.
proc.nissrv.desc: Windows Defender network protection — inspects network traffic for attacks.
proc.nissrv.tip: Part of the antivirus, leave it as is.
proc.securityhealthservice.desc: The "Windows Security" service that monitors protection status.
proc.securityhealthservice.tip: A normal process, uses almost no resources.
proc.audiodg.desc: Windows audio processing: effects, equalizer, mixing app sounds.
proc.audiodg.tip: If it loads the CPU, turn off unneeded sound effects in the sound settings.
proc.searchindexer.desc: File indexing for fast search in Windows.
proc.searchindexer.tip: May load the disk after installing programs — it will pass by itself.
proc.searchhost.desc: The Windows search window in the taskbar.
proc.searchhost.tip: A normal process, it shouldn't get in the way.
proc.runtimebroker.desc: Checks permissions of Microsoft Store apps (camera, microphone, location).
proc.runtimebroker.tip: Several copies are normal. High load is caused by some Store app.
proc.wmiprvse.desc: Answers programs' queries about the system (sensors, hardware, status).
proc.wmiprvse.tip: Load means some program polls the system often (monitoring tools, RGB software).
proc.ctfmon.desc: Language bar and text input: keyboard layouts, handwriting input.
proc.ctfmon.tip: Don't close it — switching input languages may stop working.
proc.sihost.desc: Windows shell: notifications, action center, part of the desktop.
proc.sihost.tip: Don't close it — notifications and part of the interface will disappear.
proc.spoolsv.tip: If you have no printer, the service can be disabled in "Services", but there's no need to close the process.
proc.conhost.desc: Console window for command-line programs. Starts together with them.
proc.conhost.tip: Closes by itself together with its program.
proc.dllhost.desc: A Windows helper process, e.g. for photo and video thumbnails in Explorer.
proc.startmenuexperiencehost.tip: Don't close it — the Start menu will stop opening until a restart.
proc.shellexperiencehost.desc: Parts of the Windows interface: clock, calendar, notification center.
proc.textinputhost.desc: Touch keyboard, emoji panel (Win+.) and input suggestions.
proc.applicationframehost.desc: Window frames of Microsoft Store apps (Settings, Calculator, etc.).
proc.smartscreen.desc: SmartScreen filter: warns about suspicious files and websites.
proc.smartscreen.tip: Part of Windows protection, leave it as is.
proc.vgc.desc: Riot Vanguard — the anti-cheat for Valorant and League of Legends.
proc.vgc.tip: This is an anti-cheat. Don't close it before or during a game — otherwise the game won't start or you'll be kicked from the match. After closing Vanguard you'll need to restart your PC.
proc.easyanticheat.desc: Easy Anti-Cheat — the anti-cheat of many games (Fortnite, Apex Legends, etc.).
proc.easyanticheat_eos.desc: Easy Anti-Cheat from Epic Online Services.
proc.beservice.desc: BattlEye — anti-cheat (PUBG, Rainbow Six Siege, DayZ, etc.).
proc.faceit.desc: FACEIT client and anti-cheat for Counter-Strike.
proc.chrome.desc: Google Chrome. Every tab and extension is a separate process, which is why there are so many.
proc.chrome.tip: The browser often eats the most RAM — close it before playing.
proc.msedge.desc: Microsoft Edge. It can run in the background even when the window is closed.
proc.msedge.tip: Close it before playing; turn off background running in Edge settings ("System").
proc.msedgewebview2.desc: Embedded Edge that other programs use to show their interface (Teams, widgets, etc.).
proc.msedgewebview2.tip: Closes together with the program that uses it.
proc.firefox.tip: Close it before playing to free up RAM.
proc.discord.tip: Can be closed if you're not chatting. Turn off hardware acceleration in its settings if the game stutters.
proc.steam.tip: Don't close it while playing a Steam game — the game may close. Without a game it's fine.
proc.steamwebhelper.desc: Steam's built-in browser: store, library, overlay. Several processes are normal.
proc.steamwebhelper.tip: Closes together with Steam. It uses less RAM if you enable Steam's "small mode".
proc.epicgameslauncher.tip: After the game starts, it can usually be closed.
proc.riotclientservices.desc: Riot Games client (Valorant and League of Legends launcher).
proc.riotclientservices.tip: Can be closed when you're not playing. The Vanguard anti-cheat (vgc.exe) is separate — don't touch it.
proc.telegram.tip: Safe to close — messages will still arrive on your phone.
proc.onedrive.desc: OneDrive — file sync with Microsoft cloud.
proc.onedrive.tip: Can be closed while gaming: syncing will continue after it starts again.
proc.teams.desc: Microsoft Teams — work chats and calls.
proc.teams.tip: Close it if you're not working — it uses a lot of RAM.
proc.ms-teams.desc: Microsoft Teams (new version) — work chats and calls.
proc.spotify.tip: Safe to close. If you listen while gaming, it uses few resources.
proc.nvcontainer.desc: NVIDIA driver services (control panel, updates, GeForce Experience / NVIDIA App).
proc.nvcontainer.tip: Closing is not recommended — the overlay and graphics settings may break.
proc.nvidia_overlay.desc: NVIDIA overlay (Alt+Z): video recording, screenshots, FPS counter.
proc.nvidia_overlay.tip: If you don't record video, you can close it or turn off the overlay in the NVIDIA App.
proc.nvdisplay_container.tip: Don't close it — it's needed for the NVIDIA control panel to work.
proc.lghub.desc: Logitech G HUB — settings for Logitech mice, keyboards and headsets.
proc.lghub.tip: Safe to close, but macros and lighting profiles will stop working.
proc.lghub_agent.desc: Logitech G HUB background service — applies device profiles.
proc.lghub_agent.tip: Logitech profiles won't work without it.
proc.claude.desc: Claude — an assistant app by Anthropic.
proc.claude.tip: Can be closed if you're not using it right now.
proc.python.desc: Python. Among other things, Lagnix itself runs on it (it's not shown in the list).
proc.python.tip: If you don't know what script this is, check the file path before closing it.
proc.pythonw.desc: Python without a console window — Lagnix is often started this way too.
sysinfo.xmp_help:
How to enable XMP / DOCP / EXPO:

1. Restart your PC and press Del (sometimes F2) during startup — the BIOS will open.
2. Find the XMP (Intel), DOCP (ASUS on AMD) or EXPO (AMD DDR5) option. It is usually on the main screen or in the Ai Tweaker / OC / Extreme Tweaker section.
3. Select Profile 1 (XMP I / Profile 1).
4. Save and exit: F10 → Yes.

If the PC doesn't start after that, wait: the board will return to safe settings by itself after a few attempts. Or try a lower frequency in the same menu.
sysinfo.tip.monitor_hz: Monitor "{name}" is running at {current_hz} Hz, although it supports up to {max_hz} Hz. You can enable the higher refresh rate in display settings.
sysinfo.tip.ram_xmp: Memory is running at {speed_mhz} MHz, but the modules are rated for {rated_mhz} MHz. XMP/DOCP is probably disabled in BIOS — enabling it can give +5–15% FPS in games.
sysinfo.tip.ram_single: A single memory module is installed — it runs in single-channel mode. A second identical module in the paired slot (usually A2 + B2) will enable dual-channel mode — this noticeably adds FPS, especially with integrated graphics.
sysinfo.tip.gpu_driver_old: The graphics driver hasn't been updated for about {months} months. A newer version may improve performance and stability in games.
sysinfo.tip.disk_low: Only {free_gb:.0f} GB ({free_percent:.0f}%) of free space left on drive {letter}.
sysinfo.tip.uptime: The computer hasn't been restarted for {uptime_days} days. A restart often clears accumulated slowdowns and freezes.
sysinfo.tip.power_saver: The "Power saver" power plan is active — it deliberately reduces system performance.
sysinfo.advice.cpu: The CPU was heavily loaded almost the entire check. Turn on Game Mode before playing — it closes unnecessary background programs.
sysinfo.advice.ram: There's almost no RAM left. Check Startup — maybe too many programs start together with Windows.
sysinfo.advice.disk: The disk was heavily loaded with read/write operations. Cleaning temporary files and cache may relieve it a little.
sysinfo.advice.gpu: The graphics card was working almost at its limit. If this didn't happen during a game, check whether a browser or streaming software is using the GPU.
sysinfo.advice.leader: The process "{name}" used the most resources (CPU {cpu_avg:.0f}%, RAM {ram_avg:.0f}%).
sysinfo.advice.all_good: No significant problems were found during the check — the system is in decent shape.
sysinfo.advice.tweaks: Gaming registry tweaks can add a bit of performance in games.

settings.pawnio.title: PawnIO sensor driver
settings.pawnio.hint: Without it, CPU temperature is shown as "Unavailable". An official signed driver (pawnio.eu), installed only with your consent.
settings.pawnio.confirm.title: Install the sensor driver?
settings.pawnio.confirm.text:
Lagnix will download the official PawnIO installer (github.com/namazso/PawnIO.Setup — the link from pawnio.eu), verify its digital signature and open the setup wizard. In the wizard, choose the regular (signed) edition.

The driver runs at the Windows kernel level; it can be removed via "Installed apps".
settings.pawnio.done: PawnIO is installed — CPU temperature will appear on the "Monitor" tab in a few seconds.
settings.sounds.hint: Quiet sound cues on hover, click, success and errors.
settings.game_mode.default_level.hint: For profiles whose level hasn't been chosen yet on the "Game Mode" tab.
settings.game_mode.toast.hint: "Game Mode enabled for <game>" with a "Cancel" button (5 s). If disabled, the mode turns on immediately; programs are not closed automatically either way.
settings.overlay.hint: A small semi-transparent window on top of games: CPU, GPU, RAM load and temperatures. Colors change under high load and heat.
settings.overlay.cpu_temp_hint: CPU temperature is shown only if the sensor is available (see "Monitor").
settings.overlay.drag_hint: To move the overlay, hold Ctrl and drag it with the mouse — the position will be remembered. Choosing a corner resets the saved position. Without Ctrl, the overlay passes clicks through to the game.
settings.overlay.fullscreen_hint: In fullscreen games (exclusive fullscreen) the overlay may not appear — use borderless mode.
settings.hotkeys.hint: They work everywhere, including in games. Click a field, then press a new combination (Esc — cancel).
settings.hotkeys.bad_key: this key can't be used — choose a letter, digit or F1–F24
settings.notifications.game_mode.hint: "Game Mode enabled: <game>" — when the mode turned on by itself after a game started.
settings.notifications.overheat.hint: When the temperature exceeds the threshold from the "Monitor" card — no more than once every 5 min.
settings.notifications.need_tray: Notifications are shown via the tray icon — pystray is required.
settings.interface.hint: Turn off animations if the interface lags on a weak PC.
settings.data.clear_history.title: Clear history?
settings.data.clear_history.text:
The network test history ({tests}) and game session summaries ({sessions}) will be deleted.

Settings, tweak backups and the game list will not change.
settings.data.reset.title: Reset settings?
settings.data.reset.text:
General settings (sound, interface, temperature threshold, Game Mode, etc.) will return to their defaults.

Saved initial values of registry tweaks, history and disabled startup entries will NOT change.

tweaks.preset.safe.hint: Green tweaks only — no side effects.
tweaks.preset.balanced.hint: Green + yellow ones with a small, predictable effect.
tweaks.preset.max.hint: All green and yellow. Some yellow ones only work on certain PCs and have side effects.
tweaks.preset.max.warning: The Maximum preset turns on all yellow tweaks, including those that help only on certain PCs (MPO, Nagle's algorithm, hardware GPU scheduling, Power Throttling). They may give nothing or have side effects — review the list and uncheck what you don't need. Red tweaks are not included.
tweaks.intro: Every change comes with a .reg backup and can be undone. The effect is rated honestly: most tweaks don't add FPS but remove background load and distractions.
tweaks.restore_all.hint: Roll back all tweaks changed by Lagnix to the state before the first change.
tweaks.red_never_in_presets: Red tweaks ("risky") are never included in presets — only manually, with a separate confirmation.
tweaks.windows_mode.hint: Quickly switches Windows appearance between "as usual" and "maximum performance" (tweaks of the "Appearance" section below).
tweaks.risky_ok: I understand the risk — turn it on
tweaks.preset.all_applied: All tweaks of this preset are already applied.

tweaks.preset.text: The checked tweaks will be turned on. Uncheck what you don't need. Lagnix will save a .reg backup before the change.
tweaks.all_initial: All tweaks are already in their initial state.
tweaks.restore_all.text: The checked tweaks will return to the state they were in before Lagnix first changed them.
tweaks.restore_pretty.text: Restore Windows appearance (transparency, animations, shadows) to the state before the first changes?
tweaks.apply_now.text:
To make appearance and taskbar changes take effect immediately, you can restart File Explorer (open folder windows will close). Do it now?

If you decline, the changes will apply after you sign out.
